topic.label: Governance
topic.desc: Governance of agent systems and the organisations that run them: policy, risk, compliance frameworks, access and approval, audit and provenance, privacy, safety cases and incident accountability. Extends the base Governance topic.

concepts: Writing and maintaining machine-checkable policies: scope, rules, exceptions, versioning and who owns each rule.
Identifying, rating and treating risks: registers, likelihood and impact, controls, residual risk and acceptance.
Mapping controls to frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR and HIPAA and collecting the evidence an auditor asks for.
Deciding who and which agent may do what: least privilege, approval gates, human sign-off and separation of duties.
Keeping tamper-evident records of decisions and actions: logs, signatures, lineage and the questions an audit trail must answer.
Protecting personal data: lawful basis, minimisation, retention, consent, data subject requests and breach notice.
Arguing and testing that an agent is safe enough for its use: boundaries, red lines, monitoring, kill switches and escalation.
Owning failures: incident review, blameless postmortems, decision records, change approval and rollback.
skills: Drafts a policy with scope, rules, named exceptions and an owner, written so a program could check each rule.
Finds rules that contradict each other or overlap and proposes which one should prevail and why.
Tracks each change to a policy with date, author and reason, and shows which agents ran under which version.
Builds a register of risks with owner, likelihood, impact and current controls, and keeps every rating next to its evidence.
Rates likelihood and impact on a stated scale and shows how the score changes if a control fails.
Chooses to avoid, reduce, transfer or accept each risk, records who accepted what and sets a review date.
Maps one set of controls to several frameworks so one piece of evidence can serve more than one audit.
Lists the evidence each control needs, who holds it, how fresh it is and which items are missing.
Compares current practice with a framework requirement by requirement and ranks gaps by risk and effort.
Reviews what each user and agent can reach, flags permissions never used and proposes narrower roles.
Decides which actions need a human approval, who approves, what they see and how long a request may wait.
Checks that no one person or agent can both request and approve a risky action, and lists the conflicts found.
Defines which events are logged, with what fields, for how long and who may read them, so the trail answers who, what, when and why.
Traces an output back through the data, prompts, tools and decisions that produced it and marks any link that is missing.
Checks logs for gaps, reordering and edits using hashes or signatures and reports what could not be verified.
Lists what personal data is held, where, why and for how long, and who it is shared with.
Sets how long each kind of data is kept, what is deleted or anonymised afterwards and how deletion is proven.
Walks a person's access or deletion request through verification, search, redaction and reply within the deadline.
Writes the assurance argument, in GSN style, that an agent is safe for a stated use, with the claims, evidence and known limits laid out.
Lists what an agent may observe, decide, change and call, and what stays with the host system.
Defines what is monitored, which signals page a person and how an agent is stopped or rolled back.
Writes a blameless review with timeline, causes, what worked and actions with owners and dates.
Records each significant decision with options, reasons, who decided and when it should be revisited.
Defines which changes need review, tests and a rollback plan before release and tracks approvals against them.
Records each approved exception with its owner, reason and expiry date and flags exceptions that have lapsed.
Rates a supplier or model provider on data handling, security posture and concentration risk and lists the questions it still must answer.
Schedules recurring tests of each control, records pass or fail with the date and opens a ticket when a control drifts out of compliance.
Lists who holds which permission, asks each owner to confirm or revoke it, and records the outcome and date.
Chooses a defensible sample of events or records for review and states the sampling method and the confidence it supports.
Sets how long each class of data is kept, who approves deletion and how deletion is proved afterward.
Plans adversarial tests, such as jailbreak attempts, of an agent against its stated limits, with scenarios, pass criteria and how findings are reported.
Tracks each follow-up action from an incident or audit to closure, with its owner, due date and evidence that it was fixed.
